lens: Hugging Face-style community hub: open-source persona marketplace, forks, stars, leaderboards
name: Open Practice Hub
one_liner: A community hub for call practice: forkable personas with model cards, a live coach inside every call, and evidence-backed scorecards.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the Hugging Face hub pattern: task chips, trending-first sorting, stars and forks, author credit, and a model card on every persona. Changed two things. A hub cannot coach a live call, so the call screen borrows a control-room pattern from call-tool UIs. And I rejected individual rep leaderboards as a default, since ranking reps raises consent and HR risk for team buyers. Leaderboards rank personas, scenarios and teams, and rep rankings are opt-in and measure improvement rather than absolute score.

design_language.typography: Sora 600 to 700 for display headlines and KPI numerals; Inter 400 to 600 for UI and transcript text; JetBrains Mono 500 for timers, score deltas and timestamps. All loaded from Google Fonts. Body 15px desktop, 16px on phones.
design_language.shape_and_depth: Flat first: 1px hairline borders, 14px card radius, 10px control radius, pill chips. Shadows only on floating sheets and the call HUD. Persona avatars are monogram rings with a hue hashed from the name, so 120+ personas need no stock photos. The orb survives only as the live-call presence indicator.
design_language.motion: Motion springs of 180 to 260ms for card lift and cue slide-ins. Score meters tween over 400ms and show a +delta chip. The orb pulses only while the persona speaks. Under prefers-reduced-motion, swap movement for opacity fades.
design_language.iconography: lucide-react at 1.75 stroke: 20px in controls, 16px in chips. Roles and industries use text chips, not icons, so the library stays scannable.
design_language.theme_modes: Light is the default. Dark applies on the call route and when the OS prefers dark, with a header toggle. Both modes come from the same CSS variables, with dark values listed beside each token.

navigation_and_ia: Top nav: Practice, Library, Create persona (primary button), Progress. Team appears for org roles. Right side: GitHub stars pill and Fork. Routes: /library, /library/[slug] (model card), /create (wizard), /practice/[persona] (briefing), /call/[id] (live), /debrief/[id], /progress, /team. Scenarios and personas merge into one library object, which removes the scenario dropdown. Cmd/Ctrl+K opens the palette everywhere. Phones get a bottom tab bar for Practice, Library, Create and Progress, with Team in the menu. The call route hides global nav to keep focus.

live_coaching_and_scoring: The persona stays a pure buyer, as the app already requires. A separate coach pass runs on a rolling transcript window (default GPT-4.1 mini through the OpenAI-compatible API) after each turn or on triggers: objection keywords, a 4-second silence, or a missed talk-track step. It returns typed JSON with rubric deltas, one whisper cue, an objection label with a bridge line, and the next-best question. Cues render only for the rep and never enter the persona's context. Live scores carry a live estimate label; the debrief re-grades with the full grader and quotes. Target latency is about 2 seconds behind speech. Intensity is Quiet, Standard or Strict, and a per-minute cost meter sits in the bar. No Mobbin screen I found showed live coaching, so this pattern builds on Quo's in-call bar and Delphi's transcript.
persona_library_and_wizard: Each persona is one YAML file holding the persona, scenario, rubric weights, objection tags, voice id, license and author. The library launches with a target of 120+ seeded personas across 15+ industries and about 12 roles (SDR cold call, AE discovery, insurance, mortgage, solar, home services, auto, medical devices, B2B procurement, recruiting, retail, customer success, collections). Filters: role, industry, difficulty, objection type, channel. Cards show stars, forks and a pass rate from opt-in anonymised results. Forking copies the file and records lineage. The wizard reads a job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP or pasted call, asks up to three follow-ups, cites source lines, runs a dry run, then saves privately, shares to a team, or opens a PR.
signature_moments: Rubric meters tick with deltas such as +6 Pricing the moment a criterion is covered.
A fork tree on each persona model card showing who built on whom.
A debrief replay scrubber with colored ticks where the room was lost; click to jump to the quote.
A wizard dry run that plays a 20-second cold open in the persona's voice while the form fills.
A shareable scorecard PNG with the grader model version in its footer.
openai_fund_angle: Every stage carries a model chip: Realtime voice for the persona, GPT-4.1 mini for coaching and grading, and the wizard model for persona creation. Cost per practice minute appears on the call screen. The landing page and README carry a Built on OpenAI band linking to the Realtime and API docs. The contributor path: the wizard's Open PR exports a persona file with a prefilled PR, a good first persona label marks easy entries, and a lint job validates persona files. That gives Codex a concrete role in PR review and persona maintenance, the workflow the Codex for Open Source program funds.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 1: design tokens, shadcn primitives, new shell, landing and library behind a flag, keeping current routes live. Phase 2: persona YAML data model and seeded library. Phase 3: wizard with dry run and PR export. Phase 4: coach channel on the desktop call screen, then the mobile sheet. Phase 5: debrief replay, progress and team views. Each old screen is replaced only after its successor ships.

risks: Rep leaderboards carry consent and HR risk; keep them off by default and opt-in per team.
Coach latency above about 2 seconds makes cues feel stale; spike the timing before committing to the design.
The coach must stay isolated from the persona's realtime context or the buyer may start coaching; red-team it.
Community personas can be off-brand, biased or abusive; add lint, a review queue and a license field before the library opens.
Scope is nine screens plus a wizard and a coach channel; ship the live cockpit and library first.
shadcn copy-in components add ongoing maintenance; pin the component set and document it.
Realtime minutes burn OpenAI credit quickly; the cost meter and a per-day cap are needed to plan for the fund.
